articles.title: Is Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Really the End of the Rebooted Modern Warfare Story? Infinity Ward Responds
articles.summary: Is Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 really the end of the rebooted Modern Warfare story? We asked Infinity Ward.
articles.body:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s campaign is available now in early access, and is arguably the strongest the series has been since its 2019 revival . Those who have played it will be aware that a lot of its heroes and villains meet their end in one of the darkest COD entries to date. It makes it all feel like a bow being tied on this particular storyline. Activision has confirmed a new Call of Duty subfranchise outside of the traditional Modern Warfare and Black Ops rotation is in the works, further signalling that it may be the end of this particular road.

But is that Activision’s plan, or if MW4 turns out to be a smash success, will the developer be tempted to head back to Captain Price and gang well one more time? The final mission of the campaign, taking place during the middle of the game’s credits, appears to suggest it might be the end of the line for the saga and one of its most beloved characters . It begs the question: Is this the end of the rebooted Modern Warfare story?

“It's a good question, and you'll not love the answer,” Jeff Negus, narrative director at Infinity Ward, told IGN.

“I don't know. What I do know is we tried to tell a definitive, conclusive story in that we were trying to set up, or rather pay off the setups, answer things that had been posed as questions, push characters into new territory that they've never been in before, raise the stakes, push the conflict.”

This new era of Modern Warfare started strongly with 2019’s acclaimed campaign that echoed much of what players enjoyed about the 2007 original. Despite the callbacks, the most exciting thing was that it felt like something fresh, with new characters blending in with familiar faces to tell a new story. The recently released MW4 pulls off a similar trick, weaving in a huge-scale Korean conflict with the more personal Price missions. But the path here was rocky, and not necessarily one that was meant to end here. In fact, it turns out there wasn’t really a fleshed-out idea of where the saga would go post-2019.

“No, there wasn't a long-term plan”, Negus revealed. “Similar to a television show where you got a first season, it comes out, people like it, cool, there's going to be another one. If you do it well, what you built can be built upon in a way where you can use it as a foundation and then push on top of that to build and go to new places.

“Four, that was of particular importance for us. Not many games get a four, let alone one that has these kinds of characters that have gone through the things they've gone through. And so while there wasn't a long-term plan necessarily for the story specifically from 2019, we definitely are self-reflexive in a way where we're looking back at the same time as being in the present in order to inform it and make it more impactful.”

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Campaign Screenshots

Having the plot of a four-game series being developed over the course of much of the decade not entirely mapped out is understandable, but what may be surprising is that the team didn’t know where this story would be heading just three years ago after the release of Modern Warfare 3.

“It's interesting because at the end of Modern Warfare 3, there were some definitive events that took place,” Negus explained. “And because of that, particularly for Price, once you take that action, you can't come back from it. And although it doesn't change his core motivations, and in that I don't think it changes his character, it does adjust how he tries to achieve his goals; the means changed. And we weren't beholden to it, but we wanted to use it as a way to continue the story in a meaningful way, not go, ‘Don't worry about that thing that happened,’ but really lean into it and say, ‘Well, if he had done that, it would mean this. And if it meant this, how can we use that to push into new territory?’ And that's where an alliance between Price and Valeria comes in.”

There’s a lot going on in Modern Warfare 4’s story, and it's a credit to Negus and the team that it remains coherent throughout, despite having to juggle an extensive cast dotted around much of the globe. It’s a stark contrast to MW3’s limited, plot-light campaign, which introduced fan-favourite villain Makarov in what felt like a rushed manner.

The development time granted to Infinity Ward to construct it was truncated, especially when compared to the three years it had with MW4, and it shows in its quality, but also in its quantity. This is a beefy campaign with a lot of story to tell. So much so that its opening missions almost feel like an epilogue to Modern Warfare 3, as it clears the table ahead of telling its new story. So, in an ideal world, was part of this story ever meant to be in that game from three years ago?

“Short answer, no,” Negus stated. “I think the reason that this story has so much in it is that we had the ambition to continue the legacy character storylines and a very strong impulse to return to form in that, assuming the role of a low-level soldier within a bigger war landscape. And so obviously those characters that we've been with don't really fit that desire in terms of having that perspective. So it was a challenge, but ultimately an opportunity to get to redefine our returning characters and define, for the first time, a whole set of new, young, fresh faces that would give us a totally different perspective. And we combined them together, uniting them by a common theme continuing from 2019, setting up the ‘you draw the line wherever you need it’ that permeates both threads of the storyline and both perspectives.”

This approach is definitely proving a success, with Modern Warfare 4’s campaign receiving widespread praise from fans, and a thank you from the actor behind Captain Price in return to those enjoying it. Have you played it? Did you enjoy it? Let us know in the comments!

We’ve got an in-progress Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Walkthrough to help you through the campaign missions, and a guide to All Yellow Supply Crate Locations for the 10th mission, Stranded. Make sure you don’t miss out on a thing with our guide to All Collectible Note Locations , and all the Code Solutions you’ll need to open every keypad and container.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

Here's your look at the announcement trailer for Drova 2: Torn Lands, an upcoming action RPG sequel to Drova: Forsaken Kin. Drova 2: Torn Lands will be available on Nintendo, PlayStation, Xbox, and PC (Steam and GOG).

The time has come to return to the Otherworld as the Dark Fog seems to be gone. The magic has returned to Drova, but a dangerous wound remains… a ravine that splits the lands in two. An unknown threat lingers in the depths.

The Divinities have been freed after the events of Drova - Forsaken Kin. The Dark Fog is gone. A ravine is dividing the land. It winds its way not only through the parched earth, but also through the minds of those living in the Otherworld. There are shadows in the dark. An unknown threat. Will those who live be prepared for what is about to come? Two factions, each built around their Divinity. It is up to you whom you will join: Will you choose to follow the Bear Mother or will you join the ranks of the Great Ram?

Drova 2: Torn Lands will feature a slightly larger open world, an improved and expanded combat system, two new factions, new cultures, more decisions to influence the story, and more.

articles.title: PlayStation Shadowdrops Saros Zenith Update With Boss Rush, New Game+ and Fancy Golden Crown Powerups
articles.summary: A new update for Saros dropped today, adding some new features to the hectic Housemarque shooter.
articles.body:
A new update for Saros dropped today, adding some new features to the hectic Housemarque shooter. New Carcosan Modifiers allow players to further tweak the challenge, a boss rush mode lets you compete on leaderboards, and Arjun gets a golden glow.

Zenith adds 10 new Trial Modifiers to increase the challenge level. One example is “Hostile Regeneration,” which allows you to stun larger enemies, but you have to get in and finish them with a melee strike before they recover.

The update also adds New Game+, which adds mysterious new nodes to the Armor Matrix back at Passage. You use these to move through Eclipse Layers, which ramp up the challenge with new rules and deadlier enemies.

The 100 Best PlayStation Games of All Time

During Eclipse Layers, Arjun dons a golden crown and his armor glows. The more trials you have active, the more it glows and the flashier his gilded attire gets. Wearing the crown also grants access to new story and lore entries called Visions.

Then there’s Overlord Rush, accessed via the primary unit in Passage. This is a training simulation boss rush mode that lets you take down the fiercest Saros enemies and compete for a place on global leaderboards.

“Overlord Rush is divided into multiple Sets, each of which contains a different selection of Overlords,” the post on the PS Blog said . “The Incursion and Ascension Sets contain three Overlords each, and can be completed in 10 minutes, for a nice little Saros snack. The final Set is known as Totality. As the name implies, it lines up all eight Overlords from around Carcosa in one continuous gauntlet!”

Elsewhere, Housemarque has added a bunch of accessibility modifiers for people who are struggling with Saros, including the ability to slow projectiles down, giving you more time to dodge. “You have control over how much the game slows down, and can even choose if you want the setting to kick in automatically during combat, or if you want to manually toggle it on when things get hairy,” the blog said.

There’s also a new Auto Fire setting you can toggle on, which fires your weapon for you whenever you’re aiming at an enemy. You can also change the controls to aim with the motion sensor, for players who can’t get used to patting their head while rubbing their tummy and running on a treadmill at the same time.

“We here at Housemarque are super excited for everyone to get their hands on the new content Zenith adds,” Housemarque said. “I can’t wait to hear what players think about all the new control options, see your Crown-equipped Photo mode snaps, and compete (and likely lose) to your high scores in Overlord Rush.”

Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

articles.title: Abbott & Costello Join Forces With Kolchak the Night Stalker in Horror Crossover Special
articles.summary: Comedy icons Abbott & Costello are returning to comics for the first time in half a century, and they're joining forces with none other than Kolchak the Night Stalker.
articles.body:
It's been said before, but 2026 really is the year of the bizarre comic book crossover. On top of books like Batman/Superman/Weird Al: World's Weirdest , now Monstrous Books is bringing back legendary comedy duo Abbott & Costello for a new trio of horror-themed team-up specials. Finally, these two bumbling heroes will join forces with Kolchak the Night Stalker.

With the Kickstarter campaign for Abbott & Costello Meet the Monsters now live, IGN can exclusively debut a new preview of the first issue, featuring the crossover with Kolchak. Check it out in the slideshow gallery below:

Abbott & Costello Meet the Monsters #1 Preview Gallery

Monstrous Books is releasing three new specials in all, with the other two team-ups being Abbott & Costello Meet the Morlocks and Abbott & Costello Meet Cthulu. These books mark the first new Abbott & Costello comics in more than 50 years.

Abbott & Costello Meet the Monsters #1 is written by James Aquilone, with art by Dave Acosta, colors by Zac Atkinson, letters by Taylor Esposito, and cover art by J.K. Woodward, Lukas Ketner, and Zac Atkinson.

"These six pages from Abbott & Costello Meet the Monsters #1 set the stage for the entire series," Aquilone tells IGN. "The story begins in 1943, with Bud and Lou serving in the Army. While on leave, the duo accidentally stumble through an experimental portal that sends them traveling through time."

Aquilone continues, "We thought it would be cool to open the comic in black and white, paying homage to the classic Abbott and Costello movies, then transition to full color, à la The Wizard of Oz, when the two arrive in the future. Their first stop? Las Vegas, 1972, where they'll find themselves smack in the middle of the events of the original Kolchak: The Night Stalker story. There, they'll cross paths with reporter Carl Kolchak and the vampire Janos Skorzeny. It's a fun mix of classic comedy and horror, and we can't wait to see how Bud and Lou handle Kolchak, a vampire and everything else we throw at them."

Other big crossovers revealed this year have included Judge Dredd/Biker Mice From Mars , G.I. Joe/Tomb Raider , and the mother of all crossovers, Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles .

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Formula One Has a Big AI Problem. Should the Next F1 Game Recreate It?
articles.summary: Formula One's 2026 regulation changes have introduced AI into motorsport, taking control away from drivers. Should the next F1 game replicate this or stick with "old-school" racing?
articles.body:
Since it acquired the F1 license in 2009, UK-based studio Codemasters has walked a precarious sim-cade tightrope with its F1 games. It’s never been as rigorous in its physics simulation as iRacing, rFactor or Assetto Corsa Competizione, but neither has it shied away from capturing the details and demands of the sport and packaging them up into an entertaining and ultimately rewarding race weekend.

But replicating those details will introduce a difficult new element when it comes to the next F1 game. Machine learning AI supercomputers are taking control away from Formula One drivers. Borne of the new 2026 season regulation changes, it’s a phenomenon that’s usually subtle because it works by controlling the power deployment of extremely complex hybrid power units. That’s quite tricky to eyeball from the onboard broadcast cameras. But when that AI-controlled power deployment goes wrong, it makes itself extremely conspicuous.

At a drenched Sepang circuit on the first weekend of October, race fans were treated to the sight of 22 vehicles representing the pinnacle of motorsport losing throttle and trundling at 20mph on the warmup lap. It was the result of a software glitch triggered by the wet weather and the way Sepang’s sectors are configured, and it required all teams to install a software update to their cars before the race could begin.

Lewis Hamilton, whose Ferrari came to a complete standstill on the start-finish straight, later reported that he had to do a full engine restart, essentially CTRL+ALT+DEL’ing his vehicle on the track in order to gain back some throttle control and power deployment.

One race earlier at Baku, Valtteri Bottas retired in the later stages of the race after suffering a very unusual accident. It looked as though the veteran Finn had completely missed his brake marker going into turn 15, locking up and crashing into the barriers. Only afterwards did Bottas reveal that the crash wasn’t down to driver error, but the energy deployment system.

“It was quite strange,” he told GPBlog . “On the same lap I went off in turn one, I went wide. Then I think the system’s got a bit confused. I had a huge super-clip, and then when I hit the brakes only the front brakes would work, almost like I wasn’t harvesting anymore with the rears.”

Super-clipping is another bit of autonomous driving whereby the power unit reduces throttle in order to harvest energy for the electric motor. It’s a bizarre sight and sound – a Formula One car coasting into a corner way before the braking zone, as though it’s running out of fuel.

What these incidents reveal is just how much of the 2026 F1 car is out of its driver’s control. And oddly enough it isn’t so much these obvious moments of malfunction that are the problem, it’s when things are operating as planned. That scenario’s just as damaging to the sport.

After pulling off an overtake on seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton in Suzuka earlier in the season, Lando Norris later told the official McLaren website “the battery deployment triggered, even though I didn’t really want it to, and I had to overtake Lewis as a result.

“That meant I was then a sitting duck on the next straight, where I had actually wanted to use the battery… For me, that’s taking too much control away from the driver.”

The fact that Norris could accidentally overtake 106-time race winner Lewis Hamilton, and himself feel hopeless to defend his position moments later, tells you all you need to know about how powerful the electric energy deployment is in the 2026 F1 cars, which feature about a 50:50 ratio of turbo engine and electric motor power.

It also explains why many have criticised the racing as so unnatural to watch: the power difference between a car deploying that electric power in ‘boost’ mode and a car without boost is enormous, so much so that it looks like cars from different categories racing on the same track. Or, as Charles Leclerc put it earlier this season, “ This is like the mushroom in Mario Kart .”

So you’ve got drivers openly criticising the current regulations, power units glitching out and requiring software updates before the race can go ahead, and people accidentally overtaking each other.

Now imagine you’re a developer at Codemasters watching this unfold. What do you do?

Codemasters has always put emphasis on the sport’s very specific details. Over the years, that’s meant you’ve always had to pay attention to tire wear and engine map modes, for example. In the recent games’ driver career mode, your power units become worn and using more than the allocated number over the course of a season incurs a grid penalty. You participate in Friday practice sessions to build up currency that can be used to research and manufacture new engine and aero parts.

When DRS was introduced in 2011, Codemasters also introduced it to F1 2011. Likewise ERS battery management in 2014. It’s always taken pride in simulating the minutiae of the sport, as it appears on TV screens that season, even if the simulation itself isn’t as mathematically forensic as a hardcore racing sim.

The 2026 season DLC goes some way towards capturing the current regulations. Battery deployment is an important part of racing, and there’s some nuance to how and when you harvest battery, depending on whether you’re in a straight zone, and whether your throttle is pinned above 90%. Crucially though, the game keeps you largely in control of battery harvesting and deployment unless you enable a driving aid to let the game handle it. That’s very different to the AI auto-deployment situation with its multitudinous bugs we’re seeing on the real track.

So how should F1 27 capture this energy deployment situation? It’s hard to imagine how this auto-deployment of electric power will add to your sense of satisfaction in either solo or online play, let alone how the differences between teams and their AI supercomputers might affect race outcomes. This puts the next F1 game in a fascinating position. The better a job it does of simulating Formula One, the more it will feel buggy and broken. If F1 27 goes for maximum realism, cars will slow down on straights when you’re got the throttle pinned. You’ll experience random surges in your car’s pace, and then be left feeling like you’re in a GP3 car a couple of corners later. Maybe your team-mate will trounce you because their AI deployment’s simply working better than yours.

Fans have always wanted F1 games to offer racing that’s as close to the real thing as possible until now. F1 27 might be the first time they’re genuinely ok with a developer using some creative licensing.

Best case scenario, the International Automobile Federation (FIA) bails Codemasters out from having to make that call. Planned regulation changes for the 2027 season will allow the cars’ electric power harvesting to pick up more battery during braking zones, while deploying less on straights. So the boost button should feel less like a Mario Kart mushroom, and we should see less super-clipping on straights. Should .

If the hastily compiled regulation changes work as the FIA intends, the racing in both the real sport and the 2027 game becomes a lot more orthodox. But the FIA doesn’t really know if it will work – nobody does. The fact it’s increased testing time before the season is tacit admission of that fact.

And because the season starts in March, Codemasters is going to have to react extremely quickly to the effects of those 2027 regulations. The developers are used to working fast when it comes to dialling in team and driver performance, usually having just a few race weekends to work from before the game releases. But this is more fundamental. This deployment issue dictates everything from race strategy to the basic inputs needed to control the car. Essentially, F1 27 won’t be able to commit to its handling model until Codemasters has seen the 2027 cars in action.

Of particular interest will be the online racing, which is a hinterland of bitterness and spite at the best of times, let alone when accusations of cheesing the energy deployment might carry weight. The fastest drivers in the F1 series find the meta extremely fast, and if there are exploits to be found anywhere in the setup, or in the quirks of the handling model, they’ll exploit them like a multinational corporation exploits tax loopholes. No pressure, then: just adapt to the 2027 regs, make the handling and deployment watertight for the elite players, while remaining understandable and enjoyable for the casuals. By tomorrow please, thanks.

One mode, at least, might offer something of a get out of jail card for the next release. Since F1 25, My Team mode has given you the chance to vote on proposed regulation changes at the end of each season. Usually this modifies R&D rules or cost cap, creating some exciting ‘reset’ moments for teams hoping to catch up on the development race.

But what if you were able to vote on an AI battery deployment ban? For racers looking to return to a more familiar and manual way of driving, that might be F1 2027’s best gambit. At least, until the FIA sorts the real sport out.

articles.title: GTA Recap - The Complete Timeline (Watch Before GTA 6!) - IGN
articles.summary:
Have you ever wondered how every era of the Grand Theft Auto series could actually fit together? While Rockstar has always maintained the 2D, 3D, and HD continuities are completely separate, they can't help but fill each entry with callbacks, cameos, and easter eggs., and GTA 6 will be no different. So, we’ve built the ultimate unified timeline that blends them into one massive, interconnected American crime saga. We trace the epic story of the downfall of the Forrelli crime family, chart the the explosive rise of Tommy Vercetti in 1980s Vice City, CJ's return to Los Santos, Niko Bellic's disillusionment with the American Dream in a grimy Liberty City, and the chaotic, intertwining lives of Michael, Franklin, and Trevor in the San Andreas of GTA 5. Get ready to explore the betrayals, heists, and legendary crossovers that have defined decades of gaming history: perfectly setting the stage for Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval's upcoming rampage across the modern Vice City of GTA 6.
Get ready for the next generation of Rockstar Games with this complete Grand Theft Auto timeline explainer and full series recap. In this comprehensive GTA lore video, we break down the entire history of the franchise, covering key story events across the 2D, 3D, and HD universes. Whether you're looking for a detailed GTA 5 story recap, want to understand the secret connections between iconic protagonists like Carl “CJ” Johnson, Claude, and Tommy Vercetti, or just fancy a refresher, this is the ultimate guide. articles.summary: Unlimited, renewable battery backup when the sun's out.
articles.body:
If you're in need of a super portable power station that can power your mobile electronics for days instead of hours - and then charge itself - then check out this deal. For a limited time, Amazon is offering a Daran 288Wh 600W Power Station with 80W Solar Panel Kit for $186.98 after 50% off coupon code: " L6DDL5D6 ". You don't need to be an Amazon Prime member. The kit weighs less than 20 pounds and can provide you with renewable energy when the sun's out.

50% Off the Daran 288Wh LiFePO4 Power Station and Solar Panel

Daran 288Wh 600W LiFePO4 Portable Power Station with 80W Solar Panel Kit

The Daran power station isn't a tiny pocket-sized power bank that you'd tote around every day and you can't bring it on the airplane as a carry-on (the limit is 27,000mAh). However, at just 8.9 pounds, it's lighter than most power stations and has enough juice to charge your laptop and mobile devices several times over with its generous 288Wh battery capacity.

It has a total of six charging ports, including two 120V AC outlets (600W sustained, 1200W surge), two USB-C ports (100W/30W), one USB-A port (18W), two DC5521 port (120W), and even a 12V DC charging port (aka cigarette lighter).

The power station uses LiFePO4 cells instead of lithium-ion cells you'd find in some other budget power stations and nearly all power banks. LiFePO4 cells have inherently safer chemistry, longer lifespan, and slower calendar aging than NCM cells. They are widely regarded as the best battery option for power stations.

articles.title: Save 20% Off the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset With Infinite Battery Life
articles.summary: Rated one of the best gaming headsets for 4 years running.
articles.body:
Pick up one of the best gaming headsets at a big discount ahead of Black Friday. Steelseries direct is offering the Steelseries Arctis Nova Pro wireless gaming headset for PS5 and PC for just $239.99 with free shipping when you apply coupon code " SSPOUT20 ". This headset was originally $350 when it first released back in 2022 and dropped to $300 retail when it's successor, the $400 Omni was released. It has long been one of our highest rated gaming headsets . IGN's Kevin Lee gave it a 10/10 "Masterpiece" review . I've used mine for years to the point that my earcups wore through (I replaced them with the awesome WC Freeze gel earpads ).

20% Off the Steelseries Gaming Headset With Infinite Battery Life

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset (PS5, PC)

The one feature that undoubtedly makes the Nova Pro stand out amongst the crowd is the ingenious hot-swappable battery system . The Nova Pro includes two removable, rechargeable batteries: one to use in your headset and the other to remain charged and ready to go in a base station that doubles as a charger. You get wireless freedom with zero downtime . Each battery lasts for up to 22 hours of continued use so you don't need to swap out too often.

The base station deserves additional mention. Not only does it charge your battery, it also features a clear and legible OLED display and a handy volume control knob. On the rear are USB inputs for connecting to your PC as well as an optional 3.5mm passthrough should you want to connect your speakers directly to the base station.

Of course a high end gaming headset is no good if it can't produce great sound and deliver vocal clarity. The Nova Pro is first and foremost a gaming headset, and it delivers big sound with its 40mm neodymium dynamic drivers and 360° spatial sound effects (via SteelSeries Sonar for PC, Tempest 3D Audio for PS5, and Microsoft Spatial Sound for Xbox). The retractable boom mic is clear without any static and does a great job of canceling out ambient noise. My friends regularly point out that I sound like I'm in a quiet room because they hear nothing but my voice.

The Nova Pro is comfortable to use even during gaming marathons thanks to the suspension-style headband and comfortable leatherette ear cushions. You don't have to worry about babying it either, since the headband has a steel inner core. I've tossed mine around more times than I should have and it's still functionally perfect.

articles.title: Japanese Tekken Players are Likening Tekken 6’s Rollback Netcode Mod to Serious Crimes and the Fighting Game Community is Split
articles.summary: Two weeks ago, a Tekken player created a mod that allowed users to play the game online with rollback netcode, sparking a community-wide debate between Western players and competitors based in Japan and Korea.
articles.body:
Two weeks ago, a Tekken player created a mod that allowed users to play the game online with rollback netcode, sparking a community-wide debate between Western players and competitors based in Japan and Korea.

The mod, made by a community member named Ekspym, became an instant hit among Tekken players, reaching more than 10,000 players as of October 17 and a recorded 4,547 downloads as of October 15. According to the mod’s readme, “the package contains neither the PS3 firmware nor the game,” though it acts essentially like an emulator.

It sparked a viral conversation regarding the current state of Tekken 8 (with many players seeming to prefer Tekken 6 out of the two games), but perhaps more surprisingly, received massive pushback from players in Japan and Korea.

One of the loudest voices speaking out against this mod was celebrated fighting game pro Dogura. “The pirated version of Tekken 6? That thing crosses the line way too much, and I'm horrified that no one overseas is raising negative voices about it,” he wrote in a post on Twitter/X. “When our fundamental values and sense of morality differ this much, we probably can't even have a conversation. I'm praying that the right response is taken.”

Another Japanese user named Higemura also had a viral take on the situation, worrying that the Tekken series might end due to mods such as this one. “It seems like you're running the Tekken 6 service without permission, but the people doing it should really think about what they're actually up to. If the population flows over there and money stops going to the official service, the Tekken series will come to an end, right?” they wrote .

“I totally get having an attachment to Tekken 6, since I love the bound system and move balance too, but if that's the case, you should develop a new fighting game that's Tekken 6-like. The way things are going now, you're just infringing on rights and gobbling up Bandai Namco's assets and potential customers without permission.”

Overall, it seems that Japanese players take copyright very seriously and consider such mods to be outright theft. This attitude is also reflected from some players based in Korea, with one Korean user likening it to sexual assault . (Another Japanese player even compared it to necrophilia , while another made a baffling comparison to the Civil Rights Movement .)

This, of course, prompted a massive discussion that has taken hold of the broader fighting game community. The attitudes toward such mods are far more lenient among Western players, with one writing , “Please tell me how I am supposed to ‘properly’ support the game when I cannot even buy it here? If I take a broken old bike out of the trash and repair it, why are you saying I am stealing from the bike corporation? It was trash. There was no way to buy it!”

“Explain why it is more morally righteous to demand people to pay for used copies of an old game on the secondhand market that the developers won't see any money from,” another said .

Ekspym’s Tekken 6 mod is still alive and well, and has not yet received any pushback from Bandai Namco — though it has, inadvertently, exposed a very intriguing difference in opinions about emulation and modding between Western fighting game players and those based in East Asia.

(It is worth noting, though, that some Japanese players are pushing back against this mindset, with one even pointing out a pro player using a cracked arcade cabinet in response to Dogura's initial tweet.)

This is the latest Tekken-related news to go viral after Baki’s Yujiro Hanma was finally shown off at Evo France, and he’s just as terrifying as we expected him to be.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .
